```{python}
import json

from IPython.display import display
display(pd.read_csv('results/comparison.csv'))
print(open('results/diagnostics.txt').read())
display(json.load(open('results/run-identity.json')))
```

The table numerically verifies the restricted homogeneous ideal-gas problem
against the retained independent element-potential reference. That reference
is an independent high-precision calculation, not a measured composition or
the heterogeneous answer published by Belov and Aristova (2023),
DOI 10.5541/ijot.1317496. The actual temperature, pressure, phase amount,
density, composition and native convergence/cause are retained above. Every
species, including trace ozone, retains its positive reference and native
amount. The amount rows use absolute logarithmic error; the unitless Gibbs
anchor rows and numerical closure rows use absolute error. Each metric's
unchanged tolerance is tabulated separately.

The source standard Gibbs vector, reaction and atom matrices, feed and
independent amount references are retained in
`inputs/cases/test-01/source/source.json`. The original ten-species input,
authors' commit/blob identities and both fetched and Git-normalized hashes
remain in `reference-limits.md`. Section 6 of the article gives the selected
IVTANTHERMO pressure-standard convention; the system pressure remains the
separately declared value. Native admission derives carbon and oxygen masses
from the retained Chase CO/CO2 source rows identified in the run identity.

Native unit-vector pressure-Gibbs readouts check each anchor before the solve.
The zero-heat-capacity polynomial and enthalpy/entropy anchor split encode
only the supplied Gibbs values at this temperature. No caloric quantity,
thermal derivative, variable-temperature solution or extrapolation is
qualified by that bookkeeping interval. The existing native driver owns the
single reacting solve, all trace handling, density and conservation.
Raw and classified equation rows remain separate and carry their native
row identities. Positive pressure slope and zero residual chemical potential
are checked independently of amount agreement.

Graphite and diamond remain deliberately excluded. The authors' heterogeneous
reference and solid pressure/volume conventions are unavailable; no solid
volume is invented. These separate scalar, one-state comparisons are shown
in a table without interpolation. This result supplies neither experimental
validation, global stability nor general high-temperature material properties.
Independent delivered review and manuscript promotion remain open.
